title: Nizami's Khamsa (Quintet)
summary: Nizami Ganjavi, a Persian-language poet from Ganja, composed the Khamsa, a quintet of narrative poems: a didactic poem, three romances including Layla and Majnun, and the Eskandar-nama. Encyclopaedia Iranica suggests completion dates between 1166 and 1197, with Layla and Majnun dated to 1188.

uncertainty.note: Iranica gives, on one scholar's proposal, Makhzan al-asrar likely in or shortly after 561/1166 (about a decade earlier than the usually accepted date), Leyli o Majnun in 584/1188, Eskandar-nama in 590/1194 and Haft peykar in 593/1197, noting other scholars differ.

as_recorded.value: His Layla and Majnun appeared in 1188 in his collection titled Khamsa (Quintet)

where.modern_name: Ganja, Azerbaijan (proxy pin: the poet's hometown; the sources do not name a composition place)
where.historical_name: Ganja (the sources say a Shirvanshah regime commissioned Layla and Majnun)

importance.justification: Iranica calls the Khamsa the quintet for which Nizami is universally acclaimed; its poems were later gathered in manuscript codices.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date range: Iranica gives one scholar's revised dates and says others differ; the id year 1188 is only Layla and Majnun. Pin is a proxy (Nizami's hometown Ganja). Wording on the Shirvanshah commission comes from EBSCO and is not independently confirmed.
